newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Boutros-Ghali "suspends" candidacy from UN race.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali "suspends" candidacy from UN race.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali intends to "suspend" his candidacy for re-election for the time being but has not withdrawn completely from the race for the top U.N. post, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.

Security Council president Paulo Fulci said that Boutros-Ghali intended "to suspend his candidature for the time being." But at the same time U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said he was not pulling out of the race.

In reaction to the announcement, Fulci and other council members said that this would make it possible for other African candidates to put forward their names, which they have failed to do so far. But the announcement caused immediate confusion.

Some of his supporters said Boutros-Ghali wanted to step aside only temporarily and not submit his name to another vote until he reviewed developments. The United States cast a veto against him in the Security Council on November 19 when all other 14 members supported him.
Foa told reporters "he is maintaining his candidacy, he has not withdrawn his candidacy. He simply feels there is no reason to take another vote on his candidacy."
